chunks: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the person in Ihram, can he use a comb? He said: Yes, there is no harm in it. I said to him: Can he eat the orange (citrus)? He said: Yes. I said to him: For it has a pleasant scent. He said: Indeed, the orange is food and it is not among the perfumes, so it does not contradict the first report, because he only mentioned the permissibility of eating it and did not say that smelling it is permissible, and the first report is detailed, so acting upon it is more appropriate.

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The person in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration)
key_terms.يَتَخَلَّلُ: To use a comb / to comb hair

ai.seo_question: Can a person in Ihram eat oranges or use a comb?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the distinction between food and perfume for one in Ihram, ruling that citrus fruits are permissible to eat despite their scent because they are primarily classified as food (*ta'am*) rather than perfume (*tibb*). The Imam employs the principle of *takhis* (specification), noting that the general permissibility of eating does not automatically extend to smelling, thus resolving potential contradictions in the legal texts. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on contextual classification (*hukm al-mawdu*) in deriving fiqh rulings from the Imams' statements.
